h1: Fencing in Richardson, TX: Wood, Iron, Repair and Gates
heroSub: Richardson's older ranch-house streets, alley fences and mature trees make fence jobs less simple than a catalog price. Call now and describe yours, then compare two or three written quotes.
introHtml:
Fencing in Richardson usually starts with a fence that is already there and tired. Many neighborhoods in this inner-ring suburb north of Dallas were laid out in the 1960s and 70s as ranch-house subdivisions, often with alleys behind the lots, and the wood fences along those alleys and side yards have lived through decades of North Texas storms. This page connects Richardson homeowners with independent fence contractors who quote the job. This site builds nothing itself.

Whether you are weighing repair against replacement, getting a fence back up after storm winds, or dealing with a driveway gate that quit, the honest approach is two or three comparable written quotes. Call now at (214) 555-0137 and describe the job, or read the Richardson rules below first. Any price on this page is a figure a named firm publishes, never a quote from this site.

services.title: Wood privacy fence installation
services.desc: Cedar or pine, dog-ear or board-on-board, quoted by an independent contractor. The city of Richardson sets an 8 ft maximum along the rear and side, so settle the height before you compare quotes. See wood fence installation.

services.title: Fence repair
services.desc: Leaning sections, rotted posts and missing pickets are common on older alley and side-yard runs. Ask the contractor to say plainly whether the posts or only the boards have failed. See fence repair.

services.title: Gate repair and automatic gates
services.desc: Sagging walk gates, failed latches and driveway openers that stopped moving. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license. See gate repair.

services.title: Wrought iron fences
services.desc: Tubular steel and ornamental iron for front and side yards. Richardson's city page lists a 3 ft decorative limit forward of the front wall of the house, so check that before you fall for a tall front fence. See iron fences.

sections.heading: Richardson fence rules to check before you sign
sections.html:
According to the City of Richardson's fence construction page, a permit is required to construct any fence 2 1/2 ft. in height or greater. The same page lists a permit for replacing 25% or more of a fence, for a new fence line, for extending a fence, and for pool fences. That is a much lower trigger than many neighboring cities, so a replacement that looks like routine work can still need paperwork.

On height, the city says its zoning ordinance limits fences to a maximum of 8 ft. from the rear property line to the front wall of the house. From the front wall to the front property line, the city lists 3 ft, decorative. For pool fences the city lists a minimum of 4 ft, no opening over 4 in., and self-closing, self-latching gates.

The city also states that fence contractors must be registered to perform work in Richardson. Ask any contractor for their city registration and proof of insurance, and confirm the details with the city's Building Inspection office at 972-744-4174. Your HOA may add its own rules on fence type, so get its approval in writing before work starts.

sections.heading: Older ranch lots, mature trees and expansive clay
sections.html:
Richardson's older streets have the big trees that make them pleasant, and trees are a real fence factor. Roots can push or lift posts over the years, and limbs come down on fence lines in storms. When a fence section is leaning, ask the contractor what is moving it, because replacing boards while a root or a rotted post keeps pushing is money spent twice.

Much of the Dallas area also sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture, according to TxDOT-sponsored research from UT Arlington and the Texas Transportation Institute. That research is about pavement and gives no fence-post depth, so treat any single depth you read online with caution and ask the contractor how they set posts in your soil. For a sense of storm risk, the National Weather Service counts a North Texas thunderstorm with 58 mph winds as severe.

Before anyone digs, Texas law requires you or your contractor to contact 811 two business days ahead, and Texas811 says a hired contractor is responsible for making that call. Check your plat for easements too, and ask the contractor to confirm the property line before digging. If the fence straddles the boundary and both neighbors use it, Texas Law Help says both may own it and share repair costs. That is general information, not legal advice.

sections.heading: What Richardson homeowners see in quotes
sections.html:
Fence prices vary widely, and published ranges contradict each other even within one firm. TX Fence & Deck, which serves the Dallas-Fort Worth area, advertised installed cedar privacy fence at $18 to $28 per linear foot for a standard 6 ft height on a May 2026 page. It also says board-on-board typically adds $2 to $5 per linear foot over a basic dog-ear fence. Another DFW firm, DFW Fence Contractor, advertises about $30 to $60 per linear foot for a mid-range 6 ft cedar fence, so the spread alone is a reason to get several quotes.

For repair, Roof Raiders & Co, a Dallas firm, advertises $25 to $60 per board installed and $150 to $400 for a single post pulled and reset with new concrete footing. For ornamental iron, TX Fence & Deck advertises standard tubular steel at $30 to $45 per linear foot installed. On gates, the same firm says issues caught early typically cost $100 to $300 to fix, while motor replacements can run $1,000 or more.

No Dallas-area firm's per-foot price for an 8 ft fence was found, so a contractor will have to quote that one. Ask each contractor to put materials, post spacing, gate hardware, haul-away of the old fence and the permit paperwork in writing. The fence cost guide lays out the sources.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Richardson?
faq.a: The City of Richardson says a permit is required to construct any fence 2 1/2 ft. in height or greater. The city also lists permits for replacing 25% or more of a fence, a new fence line, extending a fence and pool fences. Call the city's Building Inspection office at 972-744-4174 and check with your HOA before work starts.

faq.q: How tall can a backyard fence be in Richardson?
faq.a: The city says its Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance limits fences to a maximum of 8 ft. from the rear property line to the front wall of the house. Forward of the front wall, the city lists 3 ft, decorative. Confirm your lot with the city and your HOA, since corner lots and subdivisions can differ.

faq.q: Does a fence contractor need to be registered to work in Richardson?
faq.a: The city says fence contractors must be registered to perform work in Richardson. Texas has no state license category for fence contractors that we could find, so city registration and proof of insurance are the things to ask for. Never assume a contractor is registered because they say so; ask to see it.

faq.q: My old fence is leaning near big trees. Repair or replace?
faq.a: Ask the contractor what is moving it first, whether that is rotted posts, shifting roots or storm damage. If only boards or one section have failed, a repair may be enough, though a replacement of 25% or more of the fence triggers a Richardson permit. Get a repair quote and a replacement quote in writing and compare them side by side.
